title: Pegasus Firmamenti. Sive introductio brevis in veterum sapientiam, quae olim ab Aegyptiis & Persis Magia, hodie vero a Venerabili Fraternitate Roseae crucis Pansophia recte vocatur
shelf_note: No tradition or collection is assigned. The leaf is 1619 Latin Rosicrucian/pansophic devotional prose on the 'Light of Grace', which matches the title and author. Nothing is misplaced.
structure_note: The structure counts say pages_translated 0, but the book field says 93 and this page is translated, so one of the two instruments is wrong. Only 2 of 94 pages have a printed number, and this leaf shows none, so the single backstep is most likely a misread numeral, not a real disorder.

ocr_errors.problem: the printed v is turned into u all through the page (uestri, uocati, diuinitus, Dauid); this is a normalisation the wrong way, but the meaning is unchanged

tr_errors.english: Thus Simeon, by the prompting of the Spirit of GOD, came into the Temple of Jerusalem
tr_errors.problem: The verb is not on this page; the sentence goes on to the next leaf. 'came into' is a bridge the translator supplied. It is probably right (it matches Luke 2:27), but it is not in the source.
The fragment '-bunt' (the end of 'prophetabunt' from the previous page) is left out of the English. Only the <meta> recovers it.

other.note: The <meta> asserts what the previous page holds ('the quotation from Joel 2 and Acts 2 ...'). This is plausible from 'bunt filij uestri & filiæ uestræ', but it cannot be checked from this leaf.

missing.english: the most deceptive and plausible subtleties of Reason, which seeks to be wise beyond measure, may not be mixed in with the Light of Grace
missing.why: 'Light of Grace' set against Reason is a technical term of the pansophic and Paracelsian scheme (lumen gratiae versus lumen naturae). A general reader is not told it is a term of art.

book_verdict: The page is read and translated well. The only problems are a v→u normalisation in the OCR and a verb the translator supplied at the page seam. The notes are accurate; the Luke reference is true but goes beyond what the page names.
